text:
deploy-bot: Starting staged rollout for release v2.1.3 -> target traffic 0->30% over 45m; initial step 0->20% (eu-west-1 10%, us-east-1 10%). Change window: 2026-03-20 22:00-23:00 UTC. Tracking: https://redwood.ci/r/12345 :rocket:
ana: quick heads-up — product requests we hold at 10% if p95 latency > 250ms. @julia can you watch the latency window?
kevin: ack. I'll monitor model p95 and 5xx across regions. sending baseline probe queries now.
matt: pinned model hash `0xabc123` for this rollout to prevent auto-variant swap. added note in release notes.
julia: got it. enabling alert 'canary-latency' with threshold 240ms p95 for this rollout.
oncall-sre-bot: metric snapshot (t+5m): p95_latency=220ms, 5xx_rate=0.1%
kevin: seeing a small token-processing spike (encoder) in eu-west-1. proposes throttling eu-west back to 5% — is that a stop or temp throttle?
deploy-bot: Traffic update: set eu-west-1 -> 5% per request from kevin. Total rollout now 15%.
nana: agree with temporary throttle. product requests a 10m observation hold before any further bump.
julia: starting focused checks: running synthetic load and tailing logs. will post results in ~5m.
kevin: logs show increased GPU queue on host rwd-gpu-14 (eu-west). adding a routing override to avoid that host for canary traffic.
julia: routing rule applied, rebalanced 3 pods off rwd-gpu-14.
oncall-sre-bot: metric snapshot after routing change: p95_latency=205ms, 5xx_rate=0.08%
nana: product ok to proceed to 30% if metrics stable for 10m. propose next bump at +12m from now.
matt: canary pin still active. prepping release notes update with rollback steps and pinned hash. snippet to re-pin if needed: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/releases/12345/pin -d '{"hash":"0xabc123"}'`
kevin: ok, go for +15m bump from now. I'll have rollback script staged and ready to execute.
julia: acknowledging. will trigger a formal stop/go 3m before the bump if anything degrades.
deploy-bot: Scheduled bump to 30% in 12m (2026-03-20T22:12:34Z). Will announce a stop/go check 3m prior to that time.
nana: thanks team. :thumbsup:
